S8.01.note: The composer send button (#sp-send-btn) also uses the primary colour; the settings page is the one I traced for the button label.
steps: Click the More button at the top right of the side panel and choose Extension settings.
Click Account in the settings navigation.
Open the Autofill profile (optional) section.
Look at the Save profile button under the form: it is the filled primary-style button, and compare its label contrast with Expected.
S8.01.where: Chat tab > More (the icon button labelled More, top right) > Extension settings > Account > open Autofill profile (optional) > Save profile

S8.02.note: Configure is shown on its own in its row; I did not confirm a primary button beside it. The same secondary style is used for the Preview button in the Options section.
steps: Click More (top right of the side panel) and choose Extension settings.
Click Options in the settings navigation.
Scroll to the Keyboard shortcuts section.
Look at the Configure button: it has the bordered secondary style with a hover fill, and compare with Expected.
S8.02.where: Extension settings > Options > Keyboard shortcuts > Configure

S8.03.note: Log out uses the same danger style (opt-logout-btn in apps/extension/src/options.ts).
steps: Open More (top right) and choose Extension settings.
Click Account, then open the Autofill profile (optional) section.
Look at the Delete profile button next to Save profile: it uses the red danger style.
Do not click it on a real profile; compare the red style and label contrast with Expected.
S8.03.where: Extension settings > Account > Autofill profile (optional) > Delete profile

S8.04.note: Accessible names are set with aria-label in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts (sp-history-btn, sp-new-chat-btn, sp-menu-btn).
steps: Look at the top right of the side panel: three icon-only buttons with no visible words.
Click the clock icon; the Recent chats drawer opens.
Click Back out and click the pen icon; it starts a new chat.
Use a screen reader or hover to hear or see the name of each icon, and compare with Expected.
S8.04.where: Chat tab header (top right): the clock icon (Recent chats), the pen icon (New chat), and the More icon

S8.06.needs: an account with at least one archived chat
S8.06.note: The code does not show how a chat gets archived; the tester must archive one first from the chat's More actions menu.
steps: Click the clock icon at the top right to open Recent chats.
Look for the Archived button under the Recent chats title; it appears only when at least one chat is archived.
Click Archived and look at its pressed state (highlighted border) and the list, which switches to archived chats.
Click Archived again and compare the pressed state and list with Expected.
S8.06.where: Chat tab header > clock icon (Recent chats) > Archived

S8.07.needs: a reply that produced a runnable artifact
S8.07.note: The group has aria-label Artifact view (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/artifactPanel.ts). Preview and Code are shown only when the artifact runs in a sandbox, so a plain-text output will not show them.
steps: Look for the Outputs button in the top header of the chat view and click it.
Open an output that runs in a sandbox (for example a small web page the assistant made).
Look for the two buttons Preview and Code in the artifact panel.
Compare the grouped pair and its selected state with Expected.
S8.07.where: Chat tab header > Outputs > open a runnable output > Artifact view buttons Preview and Code

S8.08.note: The link comes from the answer text (rendered in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/markdown.ts, target _blank). The extension adds no fixed text link of its own that I found.
steps: Ask AGI a question whose answer contains a link (for example, ask it to name a website and give its address).
Look at the link in the reply: it should look different from the surrounding text.
Click the link and check that it opens its destination in a new tab.
S8.08.where: Chat tab > a reply that contains a web link

S8.09.note: Other single-line fields in the same section are City, Phone and LinkedIn URL (apps/extension/src/options.ts).
steps: Open More (top right) and choose Extension settings.
Click Account and open the Autofill profile (optional) section.
Click into the field labelled Email.
Type some text and look: the field shows the text and the label stays visible above it.
S8.09.where: Extension settings > Account > Autofill profile (optional) > Email

labels.text: How can I help you today?

S8.10.note: Shift+Enter is handled in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts (the Enter handler skips when shiftKey is set).
steps: Click in the composer box at the bottom of the Chat tab.
Type one line of text.
Press Shift+Enter to start a new line. Enter alone sends the message, so do not press it unless you want to send.
Look at the box: the cursor is on a second line and the box grows, and compare with Expected.
S8.10.where: Chat tab > the composer box with the placeholder How can I help you today?

S8.11.needs: more than 10 recent chats (the search field is hidden below that)
S8.11.note: The field appears only when the list has more than 10 chats (RECENTS_SEARCH_THRESHOLD in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts).
steps: Click the clock icon to open Recent chats.
Click the field labelled Search recent chats.
Type part of the title of a chat you have.
Look at the list: it narrows to matching chats as you type, and compare with Expected.
S8.11.where: Chat tab header > clock icon (Recent chats) > Search recent chats

S8.12.note: Searched for password input types in the app code. The only masked field found is a password input for a Clerk JWT in apps/extension/src/options.ts, which sits behind import.meta.env.DEV, so it is not in the shipped UI. No masked API-key or token field was found in the shipped side panel or settings.

S8.13.note: Searched the app for one-time-code, autocomplete one-time-code, OTP and verification code fields. The extension has no code-entry field in its own UI. It only detects one-time-code fields on other websites (apps/extension/src/features/content/elementReader.ts) and leaves them to the person (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/approvalPolicy.ts).

S8.14.needs: possibly a signed-in account (the Schedules section says No schedules on this account when empty)
S8.14.note: Weekday names come from the browser locale (weekdayLabel in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/schedulesSection.ts), so they are not in the English messages file. I did not confirm the checkbox row shows only for the chosen-days option.
steps: Open More (top right) and choose Extension settings.
Click Shortcuts in the settings navigation and find the Schedules section.
Click New schedule to open the form.
Set Repeat to On chosen days of the week and look at the row of weekday checkboxes; tick and untick one and compare with Expected.
S8.14.where: Extension settings > Shortcuts > Schedules > New schedule > choose the repeat option for chosen days of the week, then the weekday checkboxes

S8.16.note: This is a native checkbox styled as a switch (class opt-toggle), not a role=switch control. The Page assistant overlay toggle is created disabled (apps/extension/src/features/options/preference-rows.ts), so it is not a usable switch.
steps: Open More (top right) and choose Extension settings.
Click Options in the settings navigation.
Find the row labelled Task completion notifications.
Click its toggle and look: the toggle slides to on or off and the status line under it changes; compare with Expected.
S8.16.where: Extension settings > Options > Task completion notifications

S8.17.needs: a reply that produced a runnable artifact
S8.17.note: This is the same Preview and Code control as S8.07. It is hidden for outputs that do not run in a sandbox (artifactPanel.ts).
steps: Click Outputs in the top header of the chat view.
Open an output that runs in a sandbox.
Click Code, then Preview, and look at which one shows the pressed state.
Compare the two joined segments and their selected state with Expected.
S8.17.where: Chat tab header > Outputs > open a runnable output > Preview and Code toggle

S8.18.note: The native select is created in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/schedulesSection.ts. A second single-select exists in the Computer Use tab (sp-cu-mode-select: Ask first, Auto, Full access, YOLO), but that tab only appears during a browser task.
steps: Open More (top right) and choose Extension settings.
Click Shortcuts and then New schedule.
Open the Repeat drop-down and look at its options: Once, Every day, On chosen days of the week, Once a month.
Choose one option and look at the value the drop-down now shows; compare with Expected.
S8.18.where: Extension settings > Shortcuts > Schedules > New schedule > Repeat

S8.22.note: This is a native number input (type number) and the stepper is the browser's own spin button.
steps: Open More (top right) and choose Extension settings.
Click Account and open the Autofill profile (optional) section.
Click into the Years of experience field.
Press the up and down arrow keys or click the spin buttons and look: the number goes up and down by one.
S8.22.where: Extension settings > Account > Autofill profile (optional) > Years of experience

S8.29.note: The file input is a hidden input of type file (sp-attach-file-input) opened by the menu item.
steps: Click the Add attachment button at the bottom of the Chat tab.
Click Upload from device.
Choose a file in the system file picker.
Look above the composer for the attached file, and compare with Expected.
S8.29.where: Chat tab > Add attachment button in the composer > Upload from device

labels.text: How can I help you today?

S8.30.note: The drag-over state is the dragover class on #sp-composer-shell (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts). It only appears for drags that carry files.
steps: Open Finder and pick a file.
Drag the file over the composer box at the bottom of the Chat tab.
Look for the drag-over state: the border turns the accent colour and gets a glow.
Drop the file and check that it appears as an attachment; compare with Expected.
S8.30.where: Chat tab > drag a file over the composer box (the box with the placeholder How can I help you today?)

S8.31.needs: a browser task that starts a Computer Use run
S8.31.note: The tab bar is hidden on the chat view (CSS comment in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts). The exact trigger for showing it was traced only to the switchTab calls on a run start, not verified live.
steps: Send a browser task in the Chat tab so the view switches to Computer Use.
Look for the tab bar at the top with the tabs Chat and Computer Use.
Click Chat, then Computer Use, and look at which tab is underlined and selected.
Compare the selected tab with Expected.
S8.31.where: Top tab bar with Chat and Computer Use, shown after a browser task starts (Chat tab > send a browser task)

S8.33.needs: a Computer Use run that has steps
S8.33.note: The toggle sets aria-expanded (computerUsePanel.ts); the chevron rotates when expanded.
steps: Send a browser task and wait for it to run, or open the Computer Use tab after a run.
Click Assistant steps.
Look at the chevron: it turns and the step list opens.
Click Assistant steps again and compare the open and closed states with Expected.

S8.34.note: The menu may also show account rows and Open in Web when signed in with a cloud chat (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts).
steps: Click the More button at the top right.
Look at the menu: it lists Close tabs, Extension settings, Shortcuts and Help.
Press the Down arrow key to move through the items.
Compare the list and keyboard movement with Expected.
S8.34.where: Chat tab header > More (the icon button labelled More)

S8.35.needs: a web page with text to select
S8.35.note: The menu items are created in apps/extension/src/background.ts (CONTEXT_MENU_ITEMS). Rewrite selection appears only in editable fields, and Ask AGI about this page appears on a right-click on the page itself.
steps: On a web page, select a few words of text.
Right-click the selected text.
Look at the menu: it includes Ask AGI about the selected text, Explain this, Translate this and Send selected text to a local app.
Click Explain this and check that AGI opens with the selection; compare with Expected.
S8.35.where: Any web page > select some text > right-click the selection > Explain this

S8.37.note: These header buttons use the native title attribute, so the tooltip is the browser's own bubble, not a custom one. The in-page launcher on web pages has its own Ask AGI tooltip (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/launcher.ts).
steps: Move the mouse over the pen icon at the top right of the Chat tab and wait about a second.
Look for the tooltip reading New chat.
Repeat with the More icon and the clock icon.
Compare the tooltips with Expected.
S8.37.where: Chat tab header > hover over the pen icon (New chat)

S8.38.note: Escape and outside-pointer dismissal are in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/menu.ts (wirePopupMenu).
steps: Click the More button to open the menu.
Press Escape and check the menu closes and focus returns to the More button.
Open the menu again and click an empty area of the page outside it.
Check the menu closes on the outside click; compare with Expected.

S8.40.needs: a signed-in account that has at least one schedule
S8.40.note: The schedules list is built in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/schedulesSection.ts (badge at line 872) and mounted in apps/extension/src/options.ts (line 2018); the status word is shown as-is from the data, and the Options page entry point was not traced.
steps: Open the AGI extension's Options page (how it is opened was not traced in the code)
Go to the Shortcuts section and find the Schedules list
Look at the small status word beside a schedule name, for example active or failed
Compare with Expected: the status word is a small marker attached to that schedule row
S8.40.where: Options page > Shortcuts > Schedules (each schedule row shows its name and a status word beside it)

S8.41.needs: a chat filed under a project
S8.41.note: A header chip 'Project · $NAME$' with a 'Stop using this project' button exists in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts (around line 11563), but no in-extension control that files a chat into a project was found; searched 'project', 'chip' and 'tag' in apps/extension/src.

S8.42.note: No avatar image was found on finished messages; the author names 'You said:' and 'AGI said:' are screen-reader-only headings (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts, buildAuthorLabel).
steps: Sign in and open the side panel
Type any message in the composer and press send
Look at the row that says Preparing; it shows the AGI symbol mark beside the thinking dots
Compare with Expected: the assistant side is marked by the AGI symbol, and screen readers hear the headings 'You said:' and 'AGI said:' before each message
S8.42.where: Side panel > type a message in the composer and press send > the 'Preparing' row before the answer starts

S8.43.note: A determinate percent appears only while a video is being made ('Creating your video, $PERCENT$% done.'); the trigger for a video request was not traced.
steps: Sign in and open the side panel
Type a message and press send
Watch the row that says Preparing; its dots spin while the answer is prepared
Compare with Expected: an indeterminate spinner with a visible label; the row is a status region, so the label is read aloud
S8.43.where: Side panel > type a message in the composer and press send > the 'Preparing' row with spinning dots

labels.text: No response was returned. Try again.

S8.46.needs: a way to make a request fail, such as going offline
S8.46.note: The failed-answer block is built in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts (buildErrorFooter, role alert, line 316); the exact failure that produces it was not traced beyond the empty-response case.
steps: Sign in and open the side panel
Send a message that gets no answer or fails (for example while offline)
Look under the failed answer for the error text in a block with alert semantics
Compare with Expected: the block shows the message with a Retry button, and Switch model when the model menu applies
S8.46.where: Side panel > send a message and let the answer fail > the error text under the failed answer, with Retry

labels.text: Sign in to start chatting in Chrome.

S8.47.note: The strip sits above the composer, not at the top of the view; the quota warning strip (id sp-usage-warning, apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts around line 15655) uses the same placement and shows only when a usage limit is near.
steps: Open the side panel without signing in
Look at the strip just above the message box
Read the text and check the Sign in button beside it
Compare with Expected: a full-width strip with a system message and an action
S8.47.where: Side panel while signed out > strip above the composer that reads 'Sign in to start chatting in Chrome.' with a 'Sign in' button

S8.48.note: Searched apps/extension/src for 'pagination', 'loadMore', 'load-more', 'show more', 'hasMore' and 'cursor'; the only hit is apps/extension/src/background.ts (line 6096) returning hasMore for memories, and no side panel or options control reads it.

labels.text: How can I help you today?

S8.49.needs: a signed-in account and an empty chat
S8.49.note: When signed out the empty view shows only the AGI icon, the placeholder reads 'Sign in to chat' and the strip says 'Sign in to start chatting in Chrome.' (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts, renderEmptyGreeting around line 5868).
steps: Sign in and open the side panel with a new, empty chat
Look above the message box for a greeting line (it changes with the time of day and your name)
Look at the message box placeholder
Compare with Expected: a greeting and a next step (the placeholder invites a request)
S8.49.where: Side panel > first screen after signing in, with no messages yet (the empty chat)

S8.50.needs: a Chrome page the extension cannot read, such as chrome://extensions
S8.50.note: The card's description text is hard-coded English in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts (sp-blocked-desc, around line 13723), not in messages.json; the card shows when the page is restricted (side_panel.ts around line 10829).
steps: Make the active tab a Chrome page such as chrome://extensions or the Chrome Web Store
Open the AGI side panel
Look at the card titled 'Page access unavailable' at the top of the messages area
Press Retry and compare with Expected: the card gives a recovery action
S8.50.where: Open a Chrome page the extension cannot read (for example chrome://extensions) > side panel > 'Page access unavailable' card with 'Retry'
